scores.answerPreview: Think of a hash map as a highly efficient filing system where every piece of data has a unique "key" that points directly to its location. Instead of searching through every folder one by one, it uses a formula (a hash function) to jump straight to the right spot instantly. It’s essentially the fastest way to store and retrieve information when you know exactly what name or ID you're looking for.

Python is the gold standard for a reason. It reads almost like English, which means a kid doesn't get bogged down by complex syntax or "grammar" rules while they're trying to actually build something. They can focus on logic—the *how* of solving a problem—rather than fighting with where a semicolon goes.  It’s also incredibly versatile. They can make simple text games, then move into data or even basic AI concepts. It gives them a sense of power quickly because the results are immediate and clear.  If they're more of a visual/creative type, Scratch is another contender—it uses blocks to teach the same logic without typing at all. But if they want to feel like "real" hackers, Python is the way to go.
